text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Four of the world's largest alcohol producers have taken a united stand against Finnish state-owned alcohol company Alko's monopoly position.
- Health-conscious Europeans, Japanese and Americans have begun cultivating interest in the ostrich, whose dark meat contains little fat and cholestrol.
- Tax authorities in Uusimaa province gearing up for fight against billions of markka in losses in tax evasion by firms. @
- East Timorese student leader called on Finland to halt arms exports to Indonesia which she said were used against pro-democracy activists in East Timor.
- Finnish composer Joonas Kokkonen dead at 74.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Neste Oy's former oil trading chief Eija Malmivirta said the company's trading losses were based on price forecasts supported by Neste's top management, and that the company could have covered the losses. @
- Neste COO Jukka Viinanen said the company's business in Russia -- mainly petrol distribution -- was doing fairly well, but he warned against expecting Russia to open up quickly to the West.

- Steelmaker Rautaruukki Oy's CEO Mikko Kivimaki said company is "big enough" -- he was responding to British Steel chief's assessment that Rautaruukki would not survive in the long term without a partner.
- Finnish fast-food chain Hesburger challenging market leader McDonald's in Helsinki area. @
- Finnish customs plan to step up border checks on Russian trucks next week in tit-for-tat response to what they call "illegal" truck inspection practices on Russian side.
DEMARI
- Social Democrats and Conservatives worried about the opposition that has risen among Finns against EU enlargement.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Commemorative postage stamp to be issued for 100th anniversary in March 1997 of birth of the late great Olympic runner Paavo Nurmi. @
AAMULEHTI

- Bank of Finland department head Antti Suvanto says linking the currency to the ERM -- or remaining outside -- is a less dramatic matter than some have made it seem. Conditions for a stable monetary policy exist one way or the other, he said.
--Helsinki Newsroom +358-0-680 50 235
